deepdive.sec: Integrated Secondary Steel Producer with Captive Power & Downstream Value Addition

bull_bear.body: X500 Cr equity raise at ₹57.12/share (47% premium to CMP) to fund Theme 3; X350 Cr internal accruals reinvested; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on capex-driven capacity expansion, not shareholder returns; net debt-to-equity remains low at 0.16x (FY26) and targeted to fall to 0.04x by FY31.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution delays in Theme 3 (pellet, power, DRI) beyond Q3FY31; delays in Bindals revival beyond Mar'2028; iron ore/coal supply disruptions due to monsoon, mine strikes, or transport strikes; inflationary pressure on capex costs; regulatory delays in statutory clearances; competition from primary steelmakers if prices collapse; demand slowdown in infrastructure if government capex falters.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company’s ~90-day raw material inventory buffer (not finished goods) is a strategic defense against Odisha’s frequent mine strikes, transporter disruptions, and monsoon-induced ore moisture spikes — a hidden operational moat that ensures continuity, unlike peers with leaner inventories.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet at FY26 (Mar'26): net worth Rs 441 Cr, equity capital Rs 59 Cr, net D/E 0.16x; the deck frames this as 'Low leverage: Investment-grade BBB+/Stable - disciplined debt, comfortable interest coverage'.
- Credit rating BBB+/A2+ from CRISIL, Stable, reaffirmed (Jul'25) - cited as validating the credit story and enabling 'cheaper debt for incremental capex'.
- Promoter conviction cited via OCRPS subscribed at Rs 57.12 - described as a 47% premium to CMP; Optionally Convertible Redeemable Preference Shares equity conversion at Rs 57.12 happened in 2026; promoter group holds 48.9%.
- Growth funding is equity-first: fresh equity of Rs 500 Cr raised in three staggered tranches at a premium to the prevailing market price, with term debt Nil for the Rs 850 Cr project; 'Group backing: Scan Group of Industries provides a cash-flow safety net across the cycle.'
- Working capital discipline: debtor days cut from 14 to 9 (FY23 to FY26), payable days ~4, inventory days ~103 (RM ~90 / WIP ~5 / FG ~8), cash conversion cycle ~108 days, net WC ~74 days FY26; deck states inventory is raw-material-led as a buffer against ~45-day procurement lead times, mine strikes, transporter strikes and monsoon moisture.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: TMT Bars: 2.0 LTPA capacity, 82% util, branded SHRISHTII (Fe-500D/550D), Rs.43,430/ton realization; Sponge Iron: 1.5 LTPA, 84% util, 75% internally consumed; MS Billets: 2.0 LTPA, 81% util; Captive Power: 8 MW, 100% util; Pipe/Galv: 0 LTPA currently, 2 LTPA under construction; Pellet: 0 LTPA currently, 12 LTPA planned.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Described as 'Odisha's first private integrated steel producer through the secondary steel route in the mid-corporate segment', commissioned in 1996, and as Odisha's largest TMT bar manufacturer under its flagship brand SHRISHTII TMT.
- Brand-led pricing power: SHRISHTII TMT realisation shown at Rs 43,430/ton in the Odisha price hierarchy, between primary producers (est. Rs 50,000-55,000) and unbranded local (est. Rs 38,000-42,000) / spot merchant (est. Rs 36,000-40,000); the deck states the brand commands a premium of approximately Rs 1,500-2,000 per tonne over unbranded local players.
- Capital efficiency framing: 'Unlike primary producers that require large investments in upstream steel-making facilities, Scan's integrated secondary steel model delivers strong profitability with significantly lower capital deployment.'
- Distribution moat: ~99% of TMT sold direct (162,469 MT in FY26), an established multi-tier dealer/wholesaler base across Odisha with retailers contributing nearly two-thirds of sales and wholesale the remaining one-third.
- Quality credentials: IS 11786 + ISO 9001 + 14001, OHSAS 18001 certification; Fe-500/500D and Fe-550/550D grades; sizes 8mm to 32mm.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition - Bindals] Kalinga Allied Industries India Private Limited (KAII) has partnered with Scan Steels Limited to form a consortium for the acquisition and revival of Bindals Sponge Industries Limited, under IBC resolution since 2018; Bindals has a 350 TPD DRI kiln, a 12.5 MW captive power plant and five induction furnaces of 8 tons capacity to produce 1.00 Lakh MTPA of billets. SSL has infused Rs 20 Cr and KAII Rs 20 Cr toward the NCLT settlement amount, with a secured loan from Artline Commerce channelized; further overhauling, renovation and working capital to be infused 50:50 between SSL and KAII. Operations expected to resume by March 2028. A separate catalysts slide cites 'Feb 2026 - Rs 37 Cr SSL+KAII settlement by Mar 2026' and the Vision 2031 slide lists 'Bindals NCLT Integration - 350 TPD DRI + 12.5 MW + 1.0 L IF (Q4FY27)'.
- [Forward figures are estimates] The deck explicitly states 'Forward figures are management estimates, not guidance; the company expresses no view on share price.' Management estimates shown include revenue Rs 838 Cr (FY26) to Rs 1,623 Cr (FY28E) to Rs 4,133 Cr (FY31E), EBITDA Rs 49 Cr (FY26) to Rs 145 Cr (FY28E) to Rs 575 Cr (FY31E), and PAT to Rs 338 Cr (FY31E), with EBITDA margin expanding to ~13.9%.
- [Value-creation lenses] Deck presents three lenses: FY31 EBITDA potential Rs 575 Cr (DCF from the capex programme, WACC ~12%, terminal growth 4%), ~Rs 850 Cr asset base to recreate (cost to build ~17 LTPA integrated capacity at ~Rs 34,500/T plus working capital), and FY31 PAT potential Rs 338 Cr.
- [Demand backdrop] National Steel Policy targets ~300 MT capacity by FY30 (from ~200 MT) and 160 kg per-capita by FY31 vs India's ~100 kg in FY26 against world ~220+ kg; India finished-steel demand growth cited at ~8-9%; NHAI pipeline of Rs 10 L Cr through FY30 and Jal Jeevan Mission GI pipe demand named as Theme 2 drivers. Deck flags this as 'Macro context only - not a Scan forecast.'
- [Leadership succession] Promoter and Chairman Mr. Rajesh Gadodia, a Mechanical Engineering graduate from Bangalore University with 30+ years in steel; Mr. Laxminarayan Gadodia noted as next-gen 'stepping into leadership'.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 EBITDA margin: 5.9%; FY31 target: 13.9%; cost advantages: captive power (8 MW → 58 MW) reduces energy cost from ~₹6.8/kWh (grid) to ~₹4.0/kWh; low inbound logistics due to Odisha ore belt location; hot charging reduces billet reheat cost; brand premium of Rs.1,500–2,000/ton over unbranded local players; blended EBITDA/ton: ₹3,013 (FY26) → target ₹4,000+ (FY31)
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Management estimates FY28 EBITDA at X145 Cr and FY31 EBITDA at X575 Cr; strategy centers on three themes: (1) Billet expansion to 3 LTPA by Sept'26, (2) Pipe/Galv plant (2 LTPA) by Q3FY28, (3) Greenfield pellet + DRI + 50 MW power by Q3FY31; no formal guidance on share price or revenue targets beyond FY31.
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: N/A (no explicit order book disclosed; demand visibility driven by ~99% direct TMT offtake via entrenched Odisha dealer network and infrastructure tailwinds)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Bindals NCLT revival (1.0 LTPA billet + 12.5 MW power by Mar'2028) adds inorganic scale; captive pellet plant (12 LTPA) enables full upstream control; potential replication of Odisha model in other mineral-rich states; epoxy-coated TMT and structural steel offer higher-margin product extensions.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Scan Steels is an Odisha-based integrated secondary steel producer leveraging captive power, backward integration, and its dominant SHRISHTII TMT brand to drive EBITDA margin expansion from 5.9% to 13.9% by FY31, with a three-phase capex plan to scale finished capacity to 7.5 LTPA and unlock Rs.575 Cr EBITDA potential. Its low net debt-to-equity (0.16x), disciplined working capital, and entrenched distribution channel de-risk volume-led growth in India’s infrastructure-driven steel upcycle.
